title: Seventeen Point Eight Million: IOM's 2025 Reach and the Budget That's Contracting
deck: IOM provided humanitarian assistance to 17.8 million people across 170 countries and territories in 2025, shelter for 7.3 million and 4.2 million health consultations, even as global funding contracted and needs reached unprecedented levels.

title: Twenty-Six Per Cent: Afghanistan's Hunger Is Outrunning Its Funding
deck: A UN-backed assessment finds malnutrition rising across Afghanistan — an estimated 21.9 million people in need — while the country's 2026 Humanitarian Response Plan stands only 26 per cent funded.

title: Sixty-Five Per Cent: Sudan's Kordofan Displacement Surges As Funding Falls Short
deck: New displacement across Sudan's Kordofan region climbed from 132,000 people in February to over 219,000 by late June, IOM reports, as fighting spreads to new towns and donor funding fails to keep pace.

title: Seventeen Every Day: West Bank Settler Displacement and the Movement Restrictions That Enable It
deck: Over 3,200 Palestinians have been displaced across the West Bank in 2026 by settler attacks and demolitions — an average of 17 people per day, double the rate of the preceding three years. New humanitarian assessments reveal how movement restrictions and legal barriers have become the infrastructure of an ever-narrowing humanitarian space.

title: 595 Households, 14 Organisations: What Cyclone Maila’s Survivors Say About the Response
deck: Three months after Category 5 Cyclone Maila, a Pacific Humanitarian Team analysis compares what 14 organisations claim about their accountability systems with what 595 displaced households actually experienced.

title: Fewer Than Half Had a Plan: Europe’s Deadly Heatwave and the Preparedness Gap That Widened It
deck: WHO Europe convened an emergency call with 41 member states on July 6 as another heatwave built over the Atlantic. A preliminary model puts the June wave’s excess deaths near 20,400. The sharpest finding: fewer than half of those states had a national heat-health action plan when it arrived.

title: Nine Thousand in Two Weeks: Chickenpox and What Displacement Does to Disease in Gaza
deck: When the UN’s Health Cluster raised an alert for a chickenpox surge across Gaza in late June, it was tracking 9,300 cases across more than 130 health facilities in less than two weeks. The disease is not new. The conditions that made it an emergency are.

title: Forty-Three Per Cent: The Ebola Response Infrastructure That’s Being Dismantled Mid-Outbreak
deck: With 1,561 confirmed cases and 506 deaths across the DRC and Uganda, the largest Bundibugyo epidemic on record is accelerating — precisely as CDC defunding empties the laboratories and contact tracers that stopped sixteen previous outbreaks.

title: 33 Kilometres, 4,000 Families: Merapi’s Lahar Survivors Get Water Back — With El Niño on the Way
deck: Four months after a lahar flood cut off water to eleven villages, Indonesia’s national disaster agency has commissioned 33 kilometres of new pipeline — just as BMKG warns of eleven months of El Niño-driven drought ahead.

title: Eleven Hours Underground: Kyiv’s Largest Attack and the Normalization of Civilian Harm
deck: At least 21 killed, 90 injured, an ambulance station struck — and three million residents spending up to eleven hours in shelters.

title: 30 Years, 40 Credit Points: Asia Pacific Critical Care Convenes in Bali
deck: The 30th Asia Pacific Symposium on Critical Care and Emergency Medicine (APSCCEM) 2026 arrives at The Patra Bali, Kuta, July 28 – August 2 — generative AI at the bedside, teletrauma, drone-assisted response and humanitarian collaboration, three decades on.

title: 4,000 Litres at a Time: Water Bombers Over Tangerang's Burning Landfill
deck: A fire burning since June 30 at the 33-hectare Jatiwaringin landfill west of Jakarta has displaced around fifty residents — driven out by smoke, not flame. BNPB has deployed 4,000-litre water-bombing helicopters under a 14-day emergency declaration.

title: 593 Millimetres, One Month: Inside Ghana's Worst Flooding on Record
deck: Ghana recorded its highest monthly rainfall in history in June 2026, killing at least 12 people and displacing nearly 39,000 in Greater Accra alone — while a $7 million flood-alert system sat not yet switched on.

title: Nineteen Videos, One Massacre: Amnesty's Case Against the RSF in El Fasher
deck: A new Amnesty International report concludes the RSF committed crimes against humanity and ethnic cleansing during its eighteen-month siege of El Fasher, built on 45 survivor interviews and 19 verified videos of mass executions.

title: 44 Teams, 27 Countries: Venezuela's Twin Earthquakes and the Race to Pull People From the Rubble
deck: Twin earthquakes of magnitudes 7.2 and 7.5 struck northern Venezuela on 24 June 2026, killing more than 1,400 people. What followed was the largest international urban search-and-rescue deployment in the country's history — into a nation already running on empty.

title: Thirty Days Without Rain: Lombok Barat's Clean Water Emergency
deck: One month without rain has left 4,245 families across five subdistricts of Lombok Barat, West Nusa Tenggara, scrambling for clean water.

title: Four Million Daily: Syria's Bread Lifeline Has Been Cut
deck: WFP halted the nationwide bread subsidy that kept subsidised loaves within reach for four million Syrians — while the 2026 humanitarian appeal sits at just 20% funded and 7.2 million people remain acutely food insecure.

title: One Strike, One Blackout: How El Obeid Lost Its Hospitals in a Week
deck: RSF drone strikes on El Obeid's power grid in June 2026 forced dialysis centres and emergency departments to close. Next door in West Kordofan, cholera has already killed 60 people.

title: 557 Then 172: Boalemo's Floods Keep Finding the Same Houses
deck: A flash flood swept through three sub-districts in Boalemo, Gorontalo on June 18, displacing 486 people — the same villages BNPB recorded flooding fourteen months earlier. The water always recedes by nightfall. The reason it keeps returning has not.

title: 62 Casualties Before Noon: Inside Nabatiyeh's Hospitals Under Siege
deck: On June 19, a single hospital in southern Lebanon took in 25 dead and 37 wounded within hours. It is one entry in a WHO tally of 147 documented attacks on Lebanese healthcare since March — and the doctors treating the wounded have not left the building in weeks.

title: Ten Years, 1.6 Million Patients, and a Camp That No Longer Exists
deck: An international medical charity has wound down a decade of medical care in Tanzania's Nduta refugee camp, following the camp's shutdown by government order amid allegations that Burundian refugees were coerced into returning home.

title: 510 to 1: The Iran War's Bill for Global Hunger
deck: A ceasefire signed in Switzerland on June 19 ends 100 days of war between the US, Israel, and Iran. The hunger crisis it triggered — from Beirut to Mogadishu — doesn't end with it.

title: 130 Homes, 30 Hours: Aceh Barat's Flood and the Machinery Nobody Notices
deck: A river overflowed in West Aceh on June 15, flooding 130 homes and displacing 300 people. By the next day the water had receded — but the response reveals how Indonesia's disaster system actually works most weeks.

title: Gaza: While the World Counts the Dead, They Count Reasons to Keep Living
deck: A guest essay by Kamal Putra Pratama, a humanitarian medical volunteer who has served in Gaza, on what resilience really means for a population the world mostly sees through casualty counts.

title: After 703 Aftershocks: Inside Sigi's Emergency Response to Central Sulawesi's M6.7 Earthquake
deck: A magnitude 6.7 earthquake struck Central Sulawesi on June 16, 2026, killing three and displacing more than 6,400 people, with 703 aftershocks still being recorded.

title: Fifteen Per Cent: Yemen's Hunger Crisis and the Aid That Never Arrived
deck: More than 18 million Yemenis face acute hunger and the 2026 appeal is less than 15 percent funded. As the UN Security Council heard on June 16, every cut has a human cost.

title: Seven Thousand in Seven Weeks: Cholera's Rapid Rise in Northeast Nigeria
deck: Since early May 2026, a rapidly escalating cholera outbreak has infected more than 7,850 people and killed 74 across 14 local government areas in Borno State — a health system dismantled by conflict and WASH infrastructure that was already failing.

title: No Vaccine, No Playbook: Ebola Bundibugyo and the Limits of Outbreak Response
deck: When WHO declared the DRC-Uganda Ebola outbreak a PHEIC in May 2026, responders faced a hard truth: for the Bundibugyo strain, there is no vaccine and no approved treatment. The response must rely on surveillance, isolation, and community trust.

title: When Aid Withdraws: Jonglei's Suspended Operations and the Famine That Filled the Gap
deck: NGO operations suspended in South Sudan's Jonglei since March. With 30% acute malnutrition in Nyirol — double the IPC famine threshold — what happens when humanitarian access collapses entirely.

title: When the Siren Sounds Too Late: Indonesia's Flood Early-Warning Gap
deck: Medan flooded again on 5 June 2026, six months after the Sumatra disaster that killed over a thousand people and exposed deep gaps in early warning. The agencies issued their advisories on time — so why does the warning still struggle to reach the village before the water does?

title: One Drop of Humanity: What World Blood Donor Day Reveals About Indonesia's Disaster Blood Supply Gap
deck: World Blood Donor Day 2026 lands days after fresh flooding in Medan and a tsunami advisory across Sulawesi and Maluku. Blood-stock levels still aren't part of Indonesia's disaster dashboards — a look at why, and what the last-mile gap means when the next flood hits.

title: The Dashboard Delusion: What Years on the Ground Have Taught Me About AI and Disaster Response in Indonesia
deck: AI dashboards, satellite mapping, and outbreak prediction are transforming Indonesia's disaster response on paper. After years working disasters from Palu to Aceh, IHSC's Putro S. Muhammad argues the real bottleneck is the “last-mile trust gap” between what a screen shows and what local responders can act on.

title: Gaza's Water Lifeline Is Running Out: 330,000 People at Risk as Trucking Operations Wind Down
deck: OCHA reports that humanitarian partners have begun phasing out water-trucking operations across Gaza, leaving over 330,000 people at risk of losing their primary drinking water source as disease and sanitation crises deepen.

title: WADEM 2027 Paris: Call for Abstracts Now Open for the World's Premier Disaster Medicine Congress
deck: The World Association for Disaster and Emergency Medicine invites abstract submissions for its 24th Congress in Paris, 26–30 April 2027. Theme: Research, Relevance, Resilience. Deadline: 1 November 2026.

title: Buku Saku EMT: IDI dan PTBMMKI Perkuat Standar Respons Medis Darurat Indonesia
deck: Ikatan Dokter Indonesia bersama PTBMMKI meluncurkan Buku Saku EMT — panduan praktis standar tim medis darurat untuk memperkuat kapasitas respons bencana di lapangan.

title: Gaza: Aid Flows Decline 37% Even as Needs Deepen
deck: OCHA's May 2026 report documents a 37% decline in humanitarian aid flows into Gaza even as malnutrition, displacement, and health system collapse continue to worsen.

title: Syria After Assad: 16.5 Million Still in Need as Reconstruction Begins
deck: IOM's 2026 crisis response plan for Syria outlines the scale of reconstruction needs as the country transitions out of conflict, with millions still requiring humanitarian assistance.

title: When Forests Fall, Floods Rise: Lessons from Aceh's 2025 Disaster
deck: Four months after the 2025 Aceh floods, Sumatra moves from emergency response to reconstruction — raising questions about deforestation, early warning systems, and long-term resilience.

title: Iran: Flash Floods and Fragile Systems — A Compounding Crisis
deck: Flash floods across Iran exposed the fragility of emergency response systems already under strain from sanctions, infrastructure decay, and climate variability.

title: Syria's Aid Gap: What a 33% Funding Rate Tells Us About the Global Humanitarian System
deck: With only 33% of Syria's humanitarian response plan funded, the gap reveals structural failures in donor commitment, political will, and the architecture of global humanitarian finance.

title: South Africa v. Israel: What the ICJ Genocide Case Means for Humanitarian Law
deck: The genocide case before the ICJ has become the most consequential legal test of international humanitarian law in a generation, reshaping how the world defines accountability in armed conflict.

title: Climate Disasters Are Draining Southeast Asia's Shrinking Aid Budgets
deck: Humanitarian assistance for extreme weather in Southeast Asia hit a record $1.4 billion in 2023 — yet remains just 5% of total development spending, as climate-driven floods intensify and aid budgets shrink globally.
